root_cause: The cache is bypassed because cache.get(key) and cache.put(key, result.getValue()) are executed only when the argument-derived key is NOT null, so when that key is null the cache is NOT read AND NOT populated and execution falls through to an uncached invoker.invoke(invocation).

reasoning_trace.result: Lines 44-63 show the cache lookup/populate logic nested under `if (cache != null)` at line 47 and, erroneously, under `if (cache != null && key != null)` at line 49; when the inner guard is false the method falls through to the uncached `return invoker.invoke(invocation)` at line 62.

The fixed version is identical except the inner guard is removed: `cache.get(key)`, the null-value check, `cache.put(key, result.getValue())`, and `return result` now execute unconditionally inside the outer `if (cache != null)`.
The only source change is deletion of the `if (cache != null && key != null)` wrapper and re-indentation of the cache read/populate code, confirming the guard is the faulty logic.
`StringUtils.toArgumentString(Object[])` is the helper that produces the cache key from invocation arguments.
`toArgumentString` at lines 411-429 builds the key from `invocation.getArguments()`; the returned key can be null for no-argument/null-argument invocations.
Only `CacheFilter.java` and the new `CacheFilterTest.java` differ, so no other source file contributes to the fault.
`LruCache` and `JCache` are keyed by the string produced from the invocation arguments, matching the get/put path affected by the guard.
LruCache is backed by a map that accepts the argument-derived key used by CacheFilter.
JCache delegates get/put to the configured javax.cache.Cache using the same argument-derived key.

reasoning_trace: The patch adds CacheFilterTest.java with test_No_Arg_Method and test_Args_Method, which assert that repeated invocations through different invokers return the same cached value, directly exercising the get/put path that the guard can short-circuit.

Conclusion: the incorrect `key != null` condition suppresses cache usage for invocations whose argument-derived key is null; the fix removes this condition so the cache is always read and, on a miss, populated.
